key_insight: The study shows that a problem-tailored ADAPT-VQE with a full singles-doubles-triples operator pool can accurately validate a copper-site quantum chemistry workflow, cutting correlation error by over 99%.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical emulator baseline for preparing and benchmarking future quantum hardware runs on realistic transition-metal active sites such as the blue-copper center and, ultimately, laccase clusters.
method: Ran a VQE workflow on the LRZ Eviden Qaptiva emulator for the mononuclear T1 blue-copper site.
Used ADAPT-VQE with a full S+D+T operator pool to iteratively build the ansatz.
Compared results against exact diagonalisation and a hardware-efficient ansatz (HEA).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a stable energy plateau at 4.03 mEh above exact diagonalisation after selecting 148 operators, with more than 40× improvement over HEA.
watch_item: The results are emulator-based, so performance on physical quantum hardware may differ due to noise, connectivity, and compilation overhead.
paper_title: VQE Validation on the Mononuclear T1 (Blue-Copper) Site: A Stepping Stone to the Multi-Copper Laccase Cluster
